question: What is the main goal of the family planning referral method in community nursing?

options.A: To connect clients to specialized or unavailable reproductive health services
options.B: To permanently discharge clients from primary health care facilities
options.C: To reduce the overall number of children born in a specific community
options.D: To decrease the administrative workload of community health nurses

explanation: Think of a referral as a helpful bridge! When a client needs care or family planning methods that your local clinic cannot provide, you connect them to a place that can. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T6#GNS225_U3_T6_h1)

question: Why is a good referral system so important for a client's reproductive rights?

options.A: It gives nurses full authority to choose which contraceptive a client must use
options.B: It forces clients to accept permanent contraceptive methods
options.C: It prevents clients from visiting traditional birth attendants
options.D: It ensures clients can access their preferred method even if local stock runs out

explanation: Clients have the right to choose what works for their bodies. If your clinic runs out of a specific supply, referring them elsewhere protects that choice! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T6#GNS225_U3_T6_h1)

question: When should a community nurse decide to refer a family planning client?

options.A: A client requesting a routine supply of oral contraceptive pills that are currently in stock
options.B: A client experiencing severe side effects from their current method that require a doctor's care
options.C: A client who attends the clinic for her annual general wellness checkup
options.D: A client who arrives on time for a scheduled injection appointment

explanation: If a client has heavy, unusual complications beyond basic clinic care, it is safest to send them up to a doctor who can help sort it out. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T6#GNS225_U3_T6_h2)

question: A client with severe hypertension comes to your primary health post asking for combined oral contraceptive pills. What should you do?

options.A: Refer the client to a facility that offers safe, non-hormonal or progestin-only alternatives
options.B: Dispense the pills with instructions to monitor blood pressure at home
options.C: Perform a surgical tubal ligation immediately at the primary health post
options.D: Refuse service entirely and tell the client to use no protection

explanation: Combined pills contain estrogen, which isn't safe for high blood pressure. Getting her to a higher facility helps her find a safer method! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T6#GNS225_U3_T6_h2)

question: Where are surgical family planning procedures, like tubal ligation, usually performed?
explanation: Major surgeries need sterile operating theatres and specialized surgical teams found in our bigger hospitals. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T6#GNS225_U3_T6_h3)

question: What is the big advantage of organizing healthcare into different levels (primary, secondary, tertiary)?

options.A: It makes primary health clinics responsible for major surgical operations
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for any communication between nurses and doctors
options.C: It restricts rural clients from ever accessing modern contraceptive methods
options.D: It ensures clients receive care at the appropriate facility matching their medical complexity

explanation: Leveling care makes sure simple things are handled locally, while complex cases go smoothly to places fully equipped for them. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T6#GNS225_U3_T6_h3)

question: As a community nurse, what is one of your main duties before sending a client on a referral?

options.A: Providing counseling to prepare the client for the receiving facility
options.B: Punishing the client for missing previous clinic appointments
options.C: Performing major pelvic surgery at the primary clinic
options.D: Purchasing medical equipment for the tertiary hospital

explanation: A good chat beforehand calms their nerves. Counseling helps the client understand why they are going and what to expect. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T6#GNS225_U3_T6_h4)

question: Why is follow-up after a referral so important for a community health nurse?

options.A: To collect payment for the transport fare used by the client
options.B: To confirm whether the client reached the facility and received the needed service
options.C: To audit the financial records of the tertiary hospital
options.D: To reverse the contraceptive method chosen by the client

explanation: Following up lets you close the loop! You get to check if your client actually made it safely and got the care they needed. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T6#GNS225_U3_T6_h4)

question: What is the very first thing you should do when preparing a client for a family planning referral?

options.A: Send the client immediately to the hospital gate
options.B: Administer a stat dose of an emergency contraceptive
options.C: Write the referral form without speaking to the client
options.D: Establish rapport and create a confidential environment

explanation: Trust is everything in nursing. Welcoming the client warmly and ensuring privacy makes them comfortable to share and listen. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T6#GNS225_U3_T6_h5)

question: A client looks very scared about going to the general hospital to remove a contraceptive implant. How should you respond?

options.A: Cancel the referral and send the client home without protection
options.B: Scold the client for being afraid of a minor procedure
options.C: Tell her that hospitals are terrifying places and she must just endure it
options.D: Listen to her concerns, explain the procedure simply, and reassure her

explanation: Fear is completely normal. Sitting down to listen and breaking down what will happen turns anxiety into confidence. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T6#GNS225_U3_T6_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of a feedback slip in the referral process?

options.A: To notify the primary clinic about the outcome of the client's visit
options.B: To order new contraceptive commodities from the central medical store
options.C: To serve as a receipt for hospital treatment fees paid by the client
options.D: To record the daily attendance of nurses at the tertiary hospital

explanation: The feedback slip is like a reply letter! It travels back from the big hospital to tell your clinic what treatment was given. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T6#GNS225_U3_T6_h6)

question: Why should your clinic keep a duplicate copy of every referral form you write?

options.A: To replace client health records permanently with blank sheets
options.B: To prove to the government that the clinic is understaffed
options.C: To track which clients have been sent out and who needs follow-up
options.D: To ensure the client pays a fine if they lose the original paper

explanation: Keeping a duplicate helps you keep tabs on pending cases so no client gets lost along the way. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T6#GNS225_U3_T6_h6)

question: What is a major challenge that often stops clients from completing a family planning referral?

options.A: High transportation costs and distance to the receiving facility
options.B: Excessive availability of feedback slips in the primary clinic
options.C: Having too many free contraceptive options available at home
options.D: Too much emotional support provided by community health nurses

explanation: Long distances and transport money wahala are real hurdles that can discourage clients from making the trip to a secondary center. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T6#GNS225_U3_T6_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a helpful way for a nurse to handle referral barriers?

options.A: Scolding clients who complain about the distance to the referral hospital
options.B: Educating clients clearly on why the referral is necessary for their health
options.C: Linking clients with local transport schemes or community support groups
options.D: Advocating for respectful, client-friendly attitudes among hospital staff

explanation: Never scold a client! Yelling at them only drives them away from care instead of helping them solve their challenges. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T6#GNS225_U3_T6_h7)
